text:
Alex: Taking over evening shift — I'm primary for the next 8h, Priya is secondary. Leaving notes here so whoever picks up later can follow.

Priya: thanks — I can take any long-running followups after 4am UTC. 

Alex: Current hot items: 1) watch inference-router error rate (alerts: router-5xx-rate), 2) cache-service latency flapping on qgpu pool. Both have runbook pointers below.

oncall-bot: alert: router-5xx-rate fired (3m window) — severity P1 — affected: hosted-api-us-east. Pager routed to eng-oncall primary.

Marco: saw brief CPU thumps on 3 nodes last night, might be related to the kernel patch diff. If router 5xx persists, check model shard evictions (kvcache).

Alex: steps if you get the router 5xx alert: 
- check /status on inference-router: `curl -sS http://inference-router.internal/status` -> expect `ok` and `connections`
- look at router logs: `kubectl -n inference logs deploy/router --since=10m`
- if 5xx from upstream model host, run `kubectl get pods -o wide -l app=model-host` and look for `OOMKilled` or crashloop.

Priya: adding page/escalation matrix here so it's clear who to call and when: 
- P0 (service down / customer-impacting heavy): page SRE pager immediately, open bridge, @Marco + @Jana + @Taylor. 
- P1 (partial degradation, rising error rates): page eng-oncall primary (current). If no ack in 5m, escalate to secondary (Priya). If still unacked, page Marco. 
- P2 (minor perf regressions / single-customer): slack thread + oncall followup during next overlap.

Alex: quick triage thresholds we use: 
- open bridge when error rate > 10% sustained for 5m OR more than 2 customer complaints within 10m. 
- run fallback route when model-host CPU > 85% and queue length growing (see `queue_length` metric).

Jana: note on network blips — if you see a burst of `connect reset` in router logs but infra metrics look ok, enable `router.fallback_to_region=true` (temporary) in the feature flags console, that routes to the secondary region while we investigate.

Alex: how to enable fallback quickly: 
```
# temp toggle via feature API
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/flags/router.fallback_to_region" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" -d '{"value":true, "expires_in":"30m"}'
```

Taylor: customer comms guidance: if we open a bridge for >30m, DM me and I'll draft an incident status. Use the template in the runbook: https://wiki.internal/redwood/runbooks/incident-comms (link) — keep updates every 30m.

oncall-bot: incident-bridge created: https://meet.internal/bridge/abc-1729 by Alex — initial bridge note: "routing errors; fallback in progress"

Priya: quick checklist for whoever gets paged tonight: 
- confirm alert -> run the status checks above -> if OK, silence the alert and note in thread. 
- if not OK: escalate per matrix, open bridge, apply fallback toggle, collect `kubectl top` for affected pods, and capture heap/dump if OOM. 

Marco: if model-host is OOMing, try restarting the specific instance first (not full deployment): `kubectl delete pod <pod>` to let the controller spin a fresh one. If it's repeated, switch to smaller model shards or fallback model version (see Optimize -> quantization profiles).

Alex: coverage gap note — between 02:00-03:00 UTC there is only one engineer on primary in case we have an overlap gap. If something P0 occurs in that window, page both primary and secondary and ping Marco directly.

Priya: I'll be watching qgpu alarms tonight. I put an alert on `qgpu_utilization > 90% for 3m` routed to me + Alex.

Taylor: logging + post-incident: please add any commands you ran to the incident timeline in the runbook so we can turn it into a playbook if it recurs. 

Alex: +1 — I'll add the commands I ran and the metrics snapshot. If anyone needs to escalate to execs, ping me and Taylor, we'll coordinate the outreach.

Priya: thanks — leaving handoff: primary Alex, secondary Priya, pager rules in thread, runbook links posted. ping here if anything spikes. :thumbsup:

Alex: thanks — signing off until 00:30 UTC.
